stories.new_fact: AP reported that Trump and Xi are meeting at the White House today after the countries agreed to extend the current trade truce, originally expiring November 10, by two months.
stories.new_takeaway: Businesses should watch written commitments on chips, rare earths, Iran pressure and Taiwan because the extension moves the deadline but does not remove operating uncertainty.
stories.why_now: Xi arrived September 23 and the meeting is scheduled for September 24, making the truce extension and agenda live today.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent scripts covered AI diplomacy and U.S.-China incident proposals, but not this White House summit or truce extension as the national lead.
stories.uncertainty: No durable agreement was available at cutoff, and the truce extension may produce only temporary relief.
stories.watch: Written summit outcome naming goods, chip categories, rare earths, Iran pressure, Taiwan language or a changed November trade deadline.

stories.new_fact: NBC4 reported the Franklin County Engineer's Office held its annual snow-fighters roadeo Wednesday, including classroom training, skills tests, an obstacle course and new tools.
stories.new_takeaway: The local value is not the event itself but whether early crew practice turns into faster, clearer winter-road response expectations.
stories.why_now: The training happened September 23, before winter weather but close enough to the season for route and staffing preparation to matter.
stories.previous_coverage: No recent episode covered Franklin County winter road operations.
stories.uncertainty: The public report did not disclose staffing levels, route priority updates, salt inventory or measured response-time targets.
stories.watch: Franklin County route priorities, staffing updates, salt inventory and first advisory-level storm response.

stories.new_fact: MBA reported applications fell 1.5 percent for the week ending September 18, the 30-year fixed conforming rate reached 7.12 percent, ARMs rose to 9.8 percent of application activity and refinance volume fell 3 percent.
stories.new_takeaway: The operational story is ARM counseling and pipeline triage: lenders need clearer reset-risk disclosures and purchase-file reviews when fixed rates make payment math harder.
stories.why_now: MBA published the weekly survey on September 23 with data for the week ending September 18.
stories.previous_coverage: September 18 covered Freddie Mac's 6.95 percent weekly average; this episode uses the fresh MBA ARM share and application-mix workflow rather than repeating a rate recap.
stories.uncertainty: Holiday adjustment, rates and borrower mix all affect the application decline; the data does not prove lasting ARM demand.
stories.watch: Next MBA ARM share, fixed-rate movement, builder buydowns and seller-credit use in purchase files.

stories.new_fact: Paywhere announced commercial availability of a programmable banking platform for banks and credit unions to serve customers through AI assistants, applications and agents.
stories.new_takeaway: For banks, the channel decision turns on customer authentication, data-sharing scope and mandate proof when external assistants become banking doorways.
stories.why_now: The commercial availability announcement was published September 23.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent bank AI coverage focused on Deutsche Bank KYC and agentic payments; Paywhere is a vendor-channel announcement with a different consent and channel-control takeaway.
stories.uncertainty: No named financial institution, live transaction volume, completion rate, error rate, fraud outcome or customer satisfaction metric was disclosed.
stories.watch: Named bank or credit union customer, live task volume, exception rate, fraud metric, customer-consent architecture or regulator response.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Paywhere / programmable banking platform as an announced vendor-platform row for consumer and small-business servicing with compliance controls.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in the API on September 22 with published token prices, while Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5.5 the same day with a claimed 40 percent lower running cost than Opus 5.
stories.new_takeaway: The immediate frontier implication is not just model ranking; lower published prices and Work/Codex access change which enterprise pilots can be economically tested.
stories.why_now: Both primary-source model and pricing updates are dated September 22 and were uncovered for this episode.
stories.previous_coverage: September 22 covered Grok 4.7 and September 23 covered Alibaba infrastructure; this is a new price and access shift across major frontier providers.
stories.uncertainty: OpenAI pricing is checkable, but performance and total job-cost claims need third-party task-level replication; Anthropic performance comparisons are lab-reported unless external evaluators publish their own details.
stories.watch: Independent cost-per-completed-task tests, evaluator reports, enterprise access changes and any model-card or pricing update.
stories.frontier_bar: Price or access shift: published API pricing and enterprise tool access change workflow economics.

stories.new_fact: NWS forecast for the Ohio State University Airport area called for clouds early, gradual clearing, a high near 69, east wind around 9 miles per hour, and a clear night near 45.
stories.new_takeaway: The planning advice is a cool layered start, drying time for wet ground and better afternoon outdoor windows.
stories.why_now: Official local forecast was updated early September 24.
stories.previous_coverage: September 23 covered a wet planning day; today's forecast is a different, improving local weather setup.
stories.uncertainty: Microclimates and remaining wet ground may vary around Central Ohio.
stories.watch: Whether next Wednesday's shower chance strengthens in later NWS updates.
